title: Cartesian proper/open tower computes the canonical origin compositor
statement: Let F be a finite-field datum and A a finite commutative ring in Type (u+1). In the category Spaces F of finite-type schemes over F.k, let j:X→V, b:V→W, i:Y→B be open immersions, with b and i quasi-compact; let q:V→Y, p:W→B and s:B→Z be proper. Suppose b p = q i and this square is Cartesian. For every bounded-below etale-origin object K on X, the raw proper/open triangle arrow alpha of [lem-sf-composition-projection-mate] equals the canonical origin compositor of [thm-sf-comp-composition], conjugated to the factor compactifications (j,q), (i,s), and (j b,p s) by [def-sf-origin-candidate-comparison]. The factor compactifications are those of [def-sf-operation-stages]. All morphisms are over F.k; no separatedness of a structure map, tensor input, projection formula or finite Tor hypothesis is used.

proof.text: Choose an etale input E and the canonical full-origin isomorphism e:Phi(E) -> K by essential surjectivity of comparisonUpperStarPlusEtaleOrigin. Regard raw alpha as a natural transformation between the concrete three candidate functors, and apply its naturality to the underlying isomorphism e.

Map the named-map equation of finiteSiteTower.paste through the D+ inclusion. Apply cartesianTowerRestriction to compute the pro-etale tower against the source and output inclusions. Apply cartesianCandidateSiteSquare with the chosen E,K,e to compute the canonical candidate compositor against the same site boundaries, retaining the source- and target-functor images of e.

Apply the proved categorical cancel_boundary_square helper to these three equations and raw-alpha naturality. The first input comparison D is invertible by finiteSiteTower.paste; sourceInclusion is an isomorphism by construction; the source functor preserves the chosen origin isomorphism. Cancel these three epimorphisms to get the required equality on K. Both the canonical site square and the conclusion refer to the same unchanged candidateCompositor construction; no unfolding of its four factors is needed.

lean.statement:
theorem cartesianCompactSupportCompositor
    (F : WeilConjectures.FiniteFieldDatum.{u})
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    {X V W Y B Z : Spaces F}
    (j : X ⟶ V) (b : V ⟶ W) (q : V ⟶ Y) (p : W ⟶ B) (i : Y ⟶ B) (s : B ⟶ Z)
    [IsOpenImmersion ((geometry F).map j)] [IsOpenImmersion ((geometry F).map b)]
    [IsOpenImmersion ((geometry F).map i)] [QuasiCompact ((geometry F).map b)]
    [QuasiCompact ((geometry F).map i)]
    [IsProper ((geometry F).map q)] [IsProper ((geometry F).map p)]
    [IsProper ((geometry F).map s)]
    (hb : b ≫ p = q ≫ i)
    (_sq : IsPullback b.hom.left q.hom.left p.hom.left i.hom.left)
    (K : (DerivedCategory.plusEtaleOrigin (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)
      X.obj.left).FullSubcategory) :
    (alpha (ordinary F A) j b q p i s hb).app K.obj =
    ProjectionTriangleAssembly.candidateCompositor A
      (f := (j ≫ q).hom.left) (g := (i ≫ s).hom.left)
    (WeilConjectures.sixFunctorFactorCompactification j q
      ‹IsOpenImmersion ((geometry F).map j)› ‹IsProper ((geometry F).map q)›
      (j ≫ q) rfl)
    (WeilConjectures.sixFunctorFactorCompactification i s
      ‹IsOpenImmersion ((geometry F).map i)› ‹IsProper ((geometry F).map s)›
      (i ≫ s) rfl)
    (WeilConjectures.sixFunctorFactorCompactification (j ≫ b) (p ≫ s)
      (mappedCompositeOpen (geo := geometry F) j b)
      (mappedCompositeProper (geo := geometry F) p s) ((j ≫ q) ≫ (i ≫ s)) (by
        simp only [Category.assoc]
        rw [← Category.assoc q i s, ← hb]
        simp only [Category.assoc])) K
